purpose: Owner request: move the grain supply scenario towards a method that can be calibrated on Earth. This declares the method and a first pilot on the Roman pool.
what_can_and_cannot_be_calibrated_here: The Roman pool in this checkout has city sizes (official areas x sliding density), model people per cell, Roman roads, mapped rivers, coasts and relief. It has no harvests or field-labour data (they live in the missing global cache). So yield, labour and the extraction share cannot be separated. What can be estimated is their product: m = person-years of grain marketed per rural resident per year, under the assumption that marketed grain is proportional to rural people. The fantasy ledgers yield the same quantity, so the two can be compared directly.
calibration_logic: An existence test. The catalogued Roman cities existed and were fed. Under a given transport rule, the smallest m at which the model can feed them is a lower bound on how much grain the countryside marketed. A fantasy world whose m lies below that bound cannot support Roman-like cities; one far above it markets more than Rome needed.
earth_freight_network: Static 9 km grid over the Roman window, eight neighbours, edge cost = distance x mean per-km cost of the two cells, in road-km equivalents: sea 1/28, river cell (mapped water within 1.5 km) 7.5/28 (mean of the Edict's down and up rates), Roman road cell 1, other land 2. Crossing between land and sea adds 4 road-km (half a day in harbour at the sea rate). No winds, seasons, slopes or closed seas: this is a simplification of the fantasy network and is stated as such. Off-road factor sensitivities 1.5 and 3.
transport_rule: Identical code to the fantasy scenario (polity.wide_supply): delivered share 1 - c/270, cells supply their cheapest city, cities with excess ship to cities in need, cheapest link first. Limit sensitivities 135 and 540.
demand: Every catalogue city whose interval contains AD 150 on Roman land in the window. Residents = official area x sliding density; cities without an area record take the 25th percentile area of those with one (sensitivity: left out). Cities sharing a cell are summed.
supply: Rural people per cell = model people on Roman land x (1 - urban share), the urban share being total city residents over total people. Marketed grain per cell = m x rural people. Land outside the empire supplies nothing.
statistics: Fed share of city residents F(m) on the grid m = 0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.5. m95 = smallest grid m with F >= 0.95; m50 likewise. Number of cities short at each m; whether Rome is fed.
internal_transfer: West and east halves (split at the median longitude of the cities): m95 judged on the west cities alone and on the east cities alone, with the whole network operating. A method that needs very different m for the two halves is not transferable.
comparison_with_fantasy: Report the fantasy m for 10% and one third (labour-limited, sliding density) beside m50 and m95. No fantasy parameter is changed automatically by this pilot.
status_of_result: A pilot. Both pools of evidence are exposed development data; the production proxy (grain proportional to people) and the static network are the weak points. A full calibration needs Earth harvest potential and field labour on the same grid, and the seasonal sea network.
review: Independent recomputation of the network costs on a sample of city pairs with a separately written shortest-path routine, of demand and supply totals, and of F(m); byte replay.
